claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 800 MPa room-temperature yield strength.
Baseline TiVNbTa has approximately 40% room-temperature ductility.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 423 MPa compressive strength at 1273 K under 30% strain.
The proposed intervention is substitutional addition of 5–10 at% W to TiVNbTa.
Adding W to TiVNbTa will enhance lattice distortion in its BCC lattice.
Adding W to TiVNbTa will promote short-range chemical ordering.
W-induced lattice distortion and short-range ordering will stabilize the BCC phase of TiVNbTa.
The proposed W-induced structural changes will impede dislocation motion in a controlled manner.
The W addition will facilitate better dislocation mobility at approximately 1273 K.
A W addition can improve alloy compressive strength through strengthening of a BCC matrix.
Adding 5–10 at% W will improve the high-temperature yield and compressive strength of TiVNbTa at approximately 1273 K.
W-modified TiVNbTa will exceed approximately 400 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The strength improvement will occur without significant loss of ductility.
The W-modified alloy will retain thermal conductivity adequate for W-to-CuCrZr heat transfer.
Operation near 1273 K is compatible with the thermal operating limits of both adjoining W and CuCrZr components.
W is used as a plasma-facing material because of properties including high melting temperature, low sputtering rate, and low hydrogen-isotope retention.
CuCrZr is used as a heat sink because of its high thermal conductivity and strength, but its useful operating-temperature range is limited.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says W facilitates better dislocation mobility, whereas the mechanism says W-induced ordering impedes dislocation motion. No distinction between beneficial mobility and strengthening by restricted mobility is provided.

The hypothesis treats operation near 1273 K as compatible with CuCrZr limits, while the cited system evidence gives a CuCrZr working range of only 180–350 °C (approximately 453–623 K), far below 1273 K.
